RESULT: the strong conjecture is REFUTED. A connected groupoid is a K(Gamma,1), not contractible; H^2(Sk_C;D)=H^2(Gamma;M) is group cohomology, generally nonzero. Over a one-object groupoid base under (H) the merge obstruction IS the classical Schreier extension class of 1->D->K->Gamma->1, and K=C|><|D exists iff the extension splits. Witnesses with [omega]!=0: K=Z/4, D=Z/2 (Sk_C=B(Z/2), nonsplit); K=Q8, D=center (Sk_C=B((Z/2)^2), nonsplit). Dividing line is cohomological dimension (freeness), not invertibility.
